claims.say: A request is rejected when there is no token in the bucket.
claims.quote: If the bucket is empty, reject the request.

claims.say: No token in the bucket? Your request is rejected. (on-screen hook)
claims.quote: If the bucket is empty, reject the request.

claims.say: That is rate limiting: asking a client to slow down when it sent too many requests in a given amount of time.
claims.quote: The HTTP 429 Too Many Requests client error response status code indicates the client has sent too many requests in a given amount of time. This mechanism of asking the client to slow down the rate of requests is commonly called "rate limiting".

claims.say: Stripe uses rate limiters on its API (note on screen; blog title 'Scaling your API with rate limiters').
claims.quote: Scaling your API with rate limiters (title). We use the token bucket algorithm to do rate limiting.

claims.say: Stripe uses the token bucket algorithm to do rate limiting.
claims.quote: We use the token bucket algorithm to do rate limiting.

claims.say: Every Stripe user has a bucket, and each request removes one token.
claims.quote: In our case, every Stripe user has a bucket, and every time they make a request we remove a token from that bucket.

claims.say: Each request removes one token from the bucket. (scene label)
claims.quote: In our case, every Stripe user has a bucket, and every time they make a request we remove a token from that bucket.

claims.say: The server asks a client to slow down when it sends too many requests in a given amount of time. (scene label)
claims.quote: The HTTP 429 Too Many Requests client error response status code indicates the client has sent too many requests in a given amount of time. This mechanism of asking the client to slow down the rate of requests is commonly called "rate limiting".

claims.say: The 4th request finds the bucket empty, so it is rejected (worked example).
claims.quote: If the bucket is empty, reject the request.

claims.say: Tokens are added to the bucket at a steady rate.
claims.quote: You can specify a throttling rate, which is the rate, in requests per second, that tokens are added to the token bucket. You can also specify a throttling burst, which is the capacity of the token bucket.

claims.say: The user can send requests again as the bucket refills (tokens are dripped back in).
claims.quote: slowly drip more tokens into the bucket

claims.say: The rejected request can get a 429 Too Many Requests response.
claims.quote: When request submissions exceed the steady-state request rate and burst limits, API Gateway begins to throttle requests. Clients may receive 429 Too Many Requests error responses at this point.

claims.say: A Retry-After header can say how long to wait.
claims.quote: In a 429 Too Many Requests response, this indicates how long to wait before making a new request.
The HTTP 429 Too Many Requests client error response status code

claims.say: A token counts for a request.
claims.quote: API Gateway throttles requests to your API using the token bucket algorithm, where a token counts for a request.

claims.say: With a token bucket, an empty bucket is how an API says slow down (the request is rejected and the client is asked to slow down).
